scenario: [LEXP.5.11.2]: `distance.great_circle` is haversine on a sphere of radius 6 371 008.8 m with the composition fixed, every operation rounded once, and the result a `length` in `meter`. Each expected value is the clause's composition evaluated as written, operation by operation with libds's CORE-MATH sin, cos, atan2 and sqrt. Every coordinate is a `Float` slot, so each call is the runtime's. `self`: a point to itself, (10, 20) to (10, 20), is 0 m. `near`: (0, 0) to (0.45, 0), about 50 km, is 50037.7861050898 m. `anti`: (0, 0) to (0, 180), antipodal, is 20015114.442035925 m, the radius times math.pi. `west`: (10, -179) to (20, 30), a longitude near the -180 end of its range ([LEXP.5.11.1]), is 15410533.534717109 m. A longitude outside [-180, 180] is NaN's, and is `LEXP.5.11.3_bad_coordinate_never_matches`'s. A builtin that fused an operation, reassociated `a`, used another radius, or converted with a different `radians` would miss at least one value. PATH PINNED: FN_GREAT_CIRCLE in libds (`builtins.c`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
import distance

schema G scope logical:
    id: String key
    lat1: Float mutable
    lon1: Float mutable
    lat2: Float mutable
    lon2: Float mutable

rule self_is_zero:
    G g where g.id == "self" and distance.great_circle(g.lat1, g.lon1, g.lat2, g.lon2) == 0.0_m
->
    log info "self"

rule near_value:
    G g where g.id == "near" and distance.great_circle(g.lat1, g.lon1, g.lat2, g.lon2) == 50037.7861050898_m
->
    log info "near"

rule antipodal_value:
    G g where g.id == "anti" and distance.great_circle(g.lat1, g.lon1, g.lat2, g.lon2) == 20015114.442035925_m
->
    log info "anti"

rule west_value:
    G g where g.id == "west" and distance.great_circle(g.lat1, g.lon1, g.lat2, g.lon2) == 15410533.534717109_m
->
    log info "west"
